pr_title: lib: os: p4wq: add a done handler and use it to free up memory
pr_body:
This commit fixes the bug that the memory of the work request
is freed in the work handler and before it is removed from the p4wq.
This has leaded to a fatal error if the rtio i2c fallback is used frequently enough.
To fix this an additional handler is added to give the submitting code
(e.g. rtio workq) a possibility to free up dynamically allocated memory,
when it is not needed anymore by the p4wq.
This is now used in the rtio workq.

Fixes #84384

No, you'd use some other thread context to reap your workers, like e.g. polling on all the done_sem's, etc...  How that fits into your architecture is an app thing, and not all tools work perfectly.

I'm just saying that @lyakh saw and addressed seemingly the same issue already, and we should have a software system with one solution to a problem and not two.

> But do consider making it a queue-global function pointer and not per-item. Work items should be small and lean.

Just to add more context on this: The use-case where RTIO workqueue needs this is basically because there's a Mem-Slab with RTIO work items, where the P4WQ item itself is contained:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/1d441c239e325b16fa3b8e4810119eca69e337cb/subsys/rtio/rtio_workq.c#L18-L21

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/1d441c239e325b16fa3b8e4810119eca69e337cb/include/zephyr/rtio/work.h#L32-L34

The issue we're facing is that the RTIO Workqueue needs to put the item back in the pool, but there's no "reaper" context waiting to synchronize with this operation (at least not one that is exposed to the RTIO Workqueue APIs, it just knows that is RTIO). Right now the RTIO handler is putting the item back in the pool before exiting, but that is inherently racey as the P4WQ needs to finalize the item before someone else takes it and tries to submit it.

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/1d441c239e325b16fa3b8e4810119eca69e337cb/subsys/rtio/rtio_workq.c#L23-L33

issue_context.title: RTIO Workqueue - Race condition leads to dead-lock in high-demand applications
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

RTIO Workqueue has a race-condition between grabing work items from the pool and giving them back. This was pointed out by @FlorianWeber1018 where he'd run into a crash due to this service not working for submitting I2C transfer requests when stress-testing.

The underlying problem resides in P4WQ not having a way to notify once the item has been freed, as explained here (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/84322#issuecomment-2605146590).

There is a fix submitted (#84322 ), in which a callback is used now to properly free the work item before putting it back in the pool.

**Expected behavior**

There is no race-condition in pool items ownership.

**Impact**

Apps using RTIO workqueue service are prone to running into this issue. This can result in a dead-lock or a crash assuming the item submitted is never processed.
comments: Marking as low as it isn't a regression and its in-tree usage is experimental. Please override if you disagree

review_comments: The semaphore above is explicitly there to return ownership of the `w` P4WQ item back to the user, at which point they can free its memory, so accessing it again after that point doesn't seem right. If anything it should be done before, but that of course would break your use-case. So, yes, as @andyross said - two mechanisms for doing the same thing aren't good...

The semaphore is only to regain ownership of the work item and not of the whole queue right? Because the callback lives in the queue it is still in the ownership of the queue. If the semaphore is used (and in that case the done_handler must not be used) the done handler is still null and does not get called.
